'''Theodore Modis''' (born 11 August 1943) is a strategic business analyst, [[Futurists|futurist]], [[physicist]], and international consultant. He specializes in applying fundamental scientific concepts to predicting social phenomena. In particular, he uses the law of natural growth in competition as expressed by the [[logistic function]] or S-curve to forecast markets, product sales, primary-energy substitutions, the diffusion of technologies, and generally any process that grows in competition.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Modis|first1=Theodore|title=Long-Term GDP Forecasts and the Prospects for Growth|journal=Technological Forecasting & Social Change|date=2013|volume=80|issue=8|page=1557|doi=10.1016/j.techfore.2013.02.010|s2cid=55535180 |url=http://www.growth-dynamics.com/articles/Long-Term_GDP_Forecasts_WEB.pdf}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Modis|first1=Theodore|title=Life Cycles - Forecasting the Rise and Fall of Almost Anything|journal=The Futurist|date=1994|volume=28|issue=5|page=20|url=http://www.growth-dynamics.com/articles/Futurist_first.pdf}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Modis |first1=Theodore |title=Natural Laws in the Service of the Decision Maker: How to Use Science-Based Methodologies to See more Clearly further into the Future |date=July 1, 2013 |publisher=Growth Dynamics |location=Lugano, Switzerland |isbn=978-2970021681 |pages=246 |edition=1 }}</ref><ref>Modis, Theodore (2007). “Strengths and Weaknesses of S-Curves”. Technological Forecasting & Social Change. 74, (6): 866-872.</ref><ref>Debecker, Alain, and Modis, Theodore (1994). “Determination of the Uncertainties in S-curve Logistic Fits”. Technological Forecasting & Social Change. 46 (2): 153-173.</ref> He is a vehement critic of the concept of the [[technological singularity]].<ref>Modis, Theodore (2020). “Forecasting the Growth of Complexity and Change—An Update”. Published in {{cite book |last1=Korotayev |first1=Andrey |last2=LePoire |first2=David (Eds.) |title=The 21st Century Singularity and Global Futures |date=January 3, 2020 |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-3-030-33730-8 |pages=620 |edition=1|url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-030-33730-8 }} pp 101-104</ref><ref>Modis, Theodore (2012). “Why the Singularity Cannot Happen”. Published in {{cite book |last1=Eden|first1=Amnon H. et al (Eds.)|title=Singularity Hypothesis|date=2012|publisher=Springer|location=New York|isbn=978-3-642-32560-1|page=311|url=http://www.growth-dynamics.com/articles/Singularity.pdf}} pp 311-339.</ref><ref>Modis, Theodore (2006). “The Singularity Myth”. Technological Forecasting & Social Change. 73 (2): 104-112.</ref><ref>Modis, Theodore (May–June 2003). “[http://www.growth-dynamics.com/articles/futurist.pdf The Limits of Complexity and Change]”. The Futurist. 37 (3): 26-32.</ref><ref>Modis, Theodore (2002). “[http://www.growth-dynamics.com/articles/Forecasting_Complexity.pdf Forecasting the Growth of Complexity and Change]”.  Technological Forecasting & Social Change. 69 (4): 377-404.</ref> He has suggested a simple mathematical relationship between [[entropy]] and [[complexity]] as the latter being the time derivative of the former.<ref>Modis, Theodore (2022). "Links between entropy, complexity, and the technological singularity". Technological Forecasting and Social Change. Volume 176, 2022-3, p. 121457. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.techfore.2021.121457.</ref> He has argued that societal complexity may be nearing — or already at — its peak.<ref>Modis, Theodore (2025). "Complexity in the Wake of Artificial Intelligence". Complexity. Volume 2025, Article ID 7656280, 14 pages. 
https://doi.org/10.1155/cplx/7656280.</ref>

He currently lives in [[Lugano]], [[Switzerland]].

==Education==
He went to [[Columbia University]], New York, where he received a master's degree in [[Electrical Engineering]] and a Ph.D. in High Energy Physics, (sponsor [[Jack Steinberger|J. Steinberger]]). His secondary education was in Greece at [[Anatolia College]] in [[Thessaloniki]], Greece.

==Career==
Modis carried out research in [[particle physics]] at [[Brookhaven National Laboratories]] and [[CERN]] before moving to work at [[Digital Equipment Corporation]] for more than a decade as the head of a management science consultants group. He has on occasion taught at [[Columbia University]], the [[University of Geneva]], [[Webster University]], the European business schools [[INSEAD]] and [[IMD International|IMD]], and was a professor at DUXX Graduate School of Business Leadership in [[Monterrey]], Mexico between 1998 and 2001. He has been in the advisory board of the international journal [[Technological Forecasting & Social Change]] since 1991.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.journals.elsevier.com/technological-forecasting-and-social-change/editorial-board|title=Technological Forecasting and Social Change Editorial Board|via=www.journals.elsevier.com}}</ref>  He is also the founder of ''Growth Dynamics'',<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.growth-dynamics.com/ |title=Home |website=growth-dynamics.com}}</ref> a Swiss-based organization specializing in business strategy, strategic forecasting and management consulting.<ref>http://ch.linkedin.com/pub/theodore-modis/0/222/140/ {{Self-published source|date=June 2022}}</ref>

==Publications==
He has published about one hundred articles in scientific and in business journals, as well as ten books: ''Predictions'', ''Conquering Uncertainty'', ''An S-Shaped Trail to Wall Street'' (treating the [[New York Stock Exchange]] as an [[ecosystem]]), ''Predictions: 10 Years Later'', ''Bestseller Driven'', ''Natural Laws in the Service of the Decision Maker'', ''Decision-Making for a New World'', ''An S-shaped Adventure: "Predictions" 20 Years Later'', ''Fortune Favors the Bold: A Woman’s Odyssey through a Turbulent Century'',<ref>{{cite book|first=Theodore|last=Modis|title=Fortune Favors the Bold: A Woman's Odyssey through a Turbulent Century|year=2018|publisher=ibidem Press|isbn=978-3838211978}}</ref> and ''Science with Street Value: A Physicist's Wanderings off the Beaten Track''.<ref>{{cite book|first=Theodore|last=Modis|title=Science with Street Value: A Physicist's Wanderings off the Beaten Track|year=2020|publisher=ibidem Press|isbn=978-3-8382-1447-4}}</ref> His books have appeared in a number of other languages; ''Predictions'' has been translated into [[German language|German]], [[Japanese language|Japanese]], and [[Greek language|Greek]], and ''Conquering Uncertainty'' has been translated into [[Chinese Long Form]], [[Chinese Short Form]], Greek, and [[Dutch language|Dutch]]. ''Fortune Favors the Bold: A Woman’s Odyssey through a Turbulent Century'' has been translated into Greek and published under the title ''ΘΕΟΔΟΣΙΑ''.

==Distinctions==
* 2017 Certificate of Outstanding Contribution in Reviewing by the international journal [[Technological Forecasting & Social Change]]
* 1997 Outstanding-Paper-of-the-Year Award by the international journal [[Technological Forecasting & Social Change]]
* Dean's List during undergraduate at [[Columbia University]]
* First in class during High School at [[Anatolia College]]

==iPhone/iPad applications==
He has created two applications for iPhone/iPad, ''The S_Curve'' and ''Biorhythm_Science''. Together with Vasco Almeida they created applications that forecast stock prices like species by treating the stock market as an ecosystem: ''Stock Fcsts'' and ''2Stock Fcsts''<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.growth-dynamics.com/default.asp?page=software3|title=iPhone Application|website=www.growth-dynamics.com}}</ref> for the [[iPhone]] and ''Stocks' Futures'' and ''2Stocks' Future''<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.growth-dynamics.com/default.asp?page=ipad|title=iPad Application|website=www.growth-dynamics.com}}</ref> for the [[iPad]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Tqb0ykBHadQ|title=Stocks' Futures by Theodore Modis & Vasco Almeida|date=20 July 2013 |via=www.youtube.com}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Modis is the father of [[Yorgo Modis]], the grandson of [[Theodoros Modis]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1S1ZCkv2LhY/|title = The funeral of the Theodoros Modi in the Monastir(FYROM) IN 1904|website = [[YouTube]] | date=29 April 2010 }}</ref> and nephew of [[Georgios Modis]].
